transcript.text: Hi everyone. I want to get the postmortem for Tuesday's webhook incident moving. As a reminder, we had duplicate webhook events delivered to some customers for 26 minutes, triggered by a queue-worker deployment. No permanent payload loss has been confirmed. Before I can sign the remediation register, I need final status from the backend, SRE, security, and support owners per our postmortem policy. Can each of you give me an update on where you stand?

transcript.text: I need to disclose something important I found during a separate code review. While tracing the worker deployment, I discovered an undocumented retry shortcut that bypasses the webhook idempotency key on the second attempt. I confirmed this behavior only shortly before this review, which is why I haven't filed the remediation ticket yet. This is likely a contributing factor to the duplicate deliveries we saw on Tuesday and needs to be addressed in the remediation register.

transcript.text: I have something important to disclose on the SRE side. While checking an unrelated alert migration, I discovered that the duplicate-delivery alert has been disabled for ten days. Additionally, the correct alert threshold for this service is 15 minutes — which means the alert should have fired well before the 26-minute duration we saw on Tuesday. I haven't updated the monitoring ticket yet, but this needs to be captured in the remediation register since the disabled alert directly contributed to the extended impact window.
